stemBlocks.value: A pie chart shows the favourite sport of a group of students. The sector for cricket is 94°, the sector for tennis is 45° and the sector for football is x°. (i) Calculate the value of x. (ii) What percentage of the students chose cricket? (iii) Given that 40 students chose tennis, calculate the total number of students in the group.
Think first: Every pie chart rests on one fact: the sector angles add up to 360°, and each angle is the same fraction of 360° as its group is of the total.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p216-q05 from workbook page 216.

solutionSteps.instruction: Set the three sector angles equal to 360°.
Write cricket's angle as a fraction of the whole circle and convert to a percentage.
Use the tennis sector to find how many students one degree represents.

contentBlocks.value: Result: 8/9 of a student per degree

strategyBlocks.value: Subtract the two known sector angles from 360° to find x, then use the fraction angle/360 to convert cricket to a percentage and to scale the 40 tennis students up to the whole group.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: (i) x = 221  (ii) 94/360 × 100 = 26.1% (to 1 decimal place)  (iii) 320 students in the group.

whyThisWorks.value: A pie chart shares out a whole turn of 360° in the same ratio as the data, so an angle and its group are two ways of writing the same fraction. Once you know that 45° corresponds to 40 students, the constant 'students per degree' unlocks every other sector, and the full 360° gives the whole group.

commonErrors.misconception: Forgetting that the three sectors must fill the whole 360°, and solving 94 + 45 + x = 180.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Forgetting that the three sectors must fill the whole 360°, and solving 94 + 45 + x = 180.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing 40 by 360 instead of by 45 when scaling up to the total.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing 40 by 360 instead of by 45 when scaling up to the total.

commonErrors.misconception: Rounding 26.1% to 26% without being asked, or writing it as 26.1 students.

examTip.value: On any pie chart question, first write 'total = 360°' and the value of one degree in real units — most parts then take one line.
